newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Jaguar makes debut in the Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Jaguar makes debut in the Philippines.

text.p: The British-made luxury car Jaguar was formally introduced in the Philippine market on Friday.
The car's entry into the country reflects a long-term strategy at Jaguar to establish a broader presence in Asia, said Steve Watts, Jaguar Cars Exports Ltd manager for the Far East.

Jaguar Cars Ltd, 100 percent-owned by U.S.-based Ford Motor Co, had formed a joint venture and distribution agreement with Frigate Holdings and Management Corp to locally market the Jaguar line through their corporate arm Jaguar Philippines Inc.
Jaguar intends to market only 60 to 100 units yearly in the Philippines, said Wellington Soong, chairman of Frigate.
"We feel comfortable to start slowly. We just want to sell a number of vehicles relative to what we see is needed in the market," said Wellington Soong, chairman of Frigate.
He predicted annual sales of 200 by the year 2000.
Frigate Holdings is an unlisted domestic company with diverse interests in food services, property development, and dealership of communications equipment.
Jaguar would be competing with the likes of other luxury car companies such as BMW, Mercedes Benz, Volvo, Audi and Alfa Romeo.
